nodes.label: CompleteAppointmentDialog con pago al completar
nodes.rationale: El cobro y la finalizacion se hacen en el mismo dialogo porque la clienta casi siempre paga en el salon: pedirlo en el momento evita que el pago quede pendiente por olvido, y las fotos finales se publican solas en el muro al completar.

nodes.label: src/db/index.ts (db sincrono y schema)
nodes.rationale: db es sincrono (better-sqlite3) y por eso todos los helpers se pueden escribir como funciones sin async; el unico await del modulo es el fetch al BCV.

nodes.label: RegisterPaymentDialog
nodes.rationale: Un solo dialogo se reusa en /dashboard/balances y en el CRM (ClientCRMPanel) en vez de duplicar el formulario de pago: la CXC se ve desde los dos lugares, pero toda escritura pasa por la misma validacion y el mismo POST /api/payments.

nodes.label: Modulo de cuentas por cobrar (CXC)
nodes.rationale: El salon vende en credito y cobra en dolares o bolivares. La seccion /dashboard/balances muestra el total adeudado, el saldo por clienta y el historial de pagos, y permite registrar o borrar abonos. La tasa del dia se scrapea del BCV porque es la referencia real con la que cobra la clienta, y por eso el saldo se mantiene siempre en USD.

nodes.label: Guarda isAdmin en todos los endpoints nuevos
nodes.norm_label: guarda isadmin en todos los endpoints nuevos
nodes.rationale: Regla global del plan: const session = await auth(); if (!(await isAdmin(session))) return 401. Horario del salon, blockouts, pagos y saldos son herramientas internas de gestion que no significan nada para una clienta y filtrarian datos financieros ajenos; GET /api/slots y GET /api/services quedan publicos a proposito porque son el catalogo de la reserva.

nodes.label: Chequeo de pertenencia cita-cliente al registrar pago
nodes.norm_label: chequeo de pertenencia cita-cliente al registrar pago
nodes.rationale: Si el body trae appointmentId se verifica que appointments.clientId coincida con userId y se responde 400 si no. Sin esa comprobacion un pago podria imputarse a la clienta equivocada y el saldo de otra quedaria inflado o pagado.

nodes.label: Scraping de la tasa BCV desde bcv.org.ve
nodes.norm_label: scraping de la tasa bcv desde bcv.org.ve
nodes.rationale: Restriccion explicita del plan: NO usar APIs de terceros para la tasa, solo bcv.org.ve. El flujo descarga el HTML, lo guarda como .txt en tmp y lo scrapea con regex (extractBcvUsdRate -> normalizeBcvNumber), sin claves ni servicios de pago. getTodayRate cachea por dia en exchange_rates para no golpear el BCV en cada render.

nodes.label: Bloques de tiempo no disponible
nodes.rationale: Almuerzos, feriados y mantenimientos se marcan como no disponible sin tocar las citas. POST /api/blockouts devuelve 409 si el bloque se solapa con una cita existente, para no dejar una cita viva dentro de un rango que el admin cree bloqueado; GET filtra por from/to para que la agenda solo descargue el rango que esta viendo.

nodes.label: Pagos duals USD/VES con tasa del dia
nodes.norm_label: pagos duals usd/ves con tasa del dia
nodes.rationale: En Venezuela la clienta paga en Bs pero la deuda esta dolarizada. Se guarda siempre amountUsd (amountVes/rate redondeado a 2 decimales) y amountVes+rate solo cuando la moneda es VES: asi los saldos se suman en una sola moneda sin perder el monto exacto ni la tasa con la que se liquido cada abono.

nodes.label: Saldo calculado en vivo (suma de purchases menos suma de payments)
nodes.norm_label: saldo calculado en vivo (suma de purchases menos suma de payments)
nodes.rationale: No hay columna de saldo: se deriva de sum(service_purchases.servicePrice) de citas completed menos sum(payments.amountUsd). Es la unica forma de que borrar un abono o completar una cita actualice la deuda sin un job de recalculo ni estado que se desincronice; ademas el saldo siempre es consistente con las filas que lo componen.

nodes.label: Tasa del dia editable a mano
nodes.norm_label: tasa del dia editable a mano
nodes.rationale: El scrape puede fallar o el BCV puede tardar en publicar. Por eso los dialogos muestran la tasa BCV como sugerencia ('puedes corregirla') y exigen una tasa manual positiva si no se pudo obtener. POST /api/payments NO usa getTodayRate: la tasa la manda el form, para que el pago quede fiel a la tasa que realmente se aplico ese dia.

nodes.label: Referencia obligatoria en cada pago
nodes.rationale: POST /api/payments exige userId y reference no vacio (400 si falta). Sin el numero de referencia de la transferencia no hay forma de conciliar un abono parcial con la clienta ni de defenderse de un cobro duplicado: es el mismo dato que pide el voucher del banco.

nodes.label: Seeds re-ejecutables de horario y pagos demo
nodes.norm_label: seeds re-ejecutables de horario y pagos demo
nodes.rationale: db:seed:client siembra working_hours solo si la tabla esta vacia (nunca pisa lo que configuro el admin) y borra los pagos del demo antes de recrearlos, porque al borrar citas appointments queda huerfano en payments. Los pagos demo (PAGO-001 $35, PAGO-002 $10) dejan el resto de una cita completada como deuda para poder probar la CXC con saldo real.

nodes.label: Validacion de disponibilidad en el servidor
nodes.norm_label: validacion de disponibilidad en el servidor
nodes.rationale: La agenda de la clienta y la del admin comparten una unica funcion validateSlot(startTime, endTime) que devuelve un mensaje o null. Centralizarla evita que el doble booking dependa de lo que el navegador ya renderizo y cubre en un solo lugar: pasado, dia cerrado, fuera de horario, solape con cita y solape con blockout. El POST responde 409 con ese mensaje, que la UI muestra tal cual.

nodes.label: Snapshot inmutable del servicio al comprar (service_purchases)
nodes.norm_label: snapshot inmutable del servicio al comprar (service_purchases)
nodes.rationale: Al crear la cita se congela serviceName/serviceDescription/servicePrice/serviceDurationMins en service_purchases. El saldo se suma sobre ese snapshot y no sobre services, para que subir el precio de un servicio no altere las deudas ya contraidas ni el historial de lo cobrado.

nodes.label: Timezone America/Caracas (UTC-4 fijo)
nodes.rationale: TODAS las fechas se convierten con el patron new Date(date + 'T00:00:00-04:00') y con Intl timeZone America/Caracas. El salon opera en Venezuela y el servidor puede estar en otra zona, asi que el offset -04:00 se fija de forma explicita en vez de depender de la zona del proceso: evita que un slot caiga en el dia anterior y que las citas del dia se filtren mal.

nodes.label: Citas para walk-ins creadas por el admin
nodes.norm_label: citas para walk-ins creadas por el admin
nodes.rationale: El salon necesita agendar clientas que nunca se registran (WhatsApp, referidas). En vez de inventar un modelo de datos aparte, el admin elige o crea un usuario y manda clientId; el POST /api/appointments solo exige isAdmin cuando viene clientId, de modo que el flujo publico de autoservicio queda intacto y el walk-in igual genera cita, fotos y snapshot de compra.

nodes.label: Horario de trabajo configurable por dia de la semana
nodes.norm_label: horario de trabajo configurable por dia de la semana
nodes.rationale: El 09:00-18:00 estaba hardcodeado en generateSlots. Ahora la tabla working_hours por dia alimenta generateSlots via openMin/closeMin, y getWorkingHoursAll completa los 7 dias con DEFAULT_WORKING_HOURS (Lun-Sab 09:00-18:00, Dom cerrado) cuando falta una fila: una tabla vacia no puede cerrar el salon ni devolver cero slots.

nodes.label: Plan: citas admin walk-ins, horario de trabajo, cuentas por cobrar y pagos
nodes.norm_label: plan: citas admin walk-ins, horario de trabajo, cuentas por cobrar y pagos

nodes.label: User Activity Log Module (Audit Log)
nodes.rationale: Goal: record every system mutation in a generic activity_logs table (who, what, when) and surface it in a dashboard page with filters and pagination. The design is a single generic table plus one synchronous helper called from ~45 mutating endpoints right after the successful mutation, rather than per-module audit tables, so the audit trail is uniform and queryable from one place.

nodes.label: activityLog permission key
nodes.rationale: Audit data is sensitive (it names users and their actions), so both read endpoints and the page are gated by a dedicated `activityLog` admin permission instead of being visible to any admin.

nodes.label: AuditEntity / AUDIT_ENTITIES union
nodes.rationale: The entity union is a closed list of module names that doubles as the whitelist of auditable modules. It was deliberately widened beyond the spec with brand_settings, nav_items and legal_settings so identity, navigation and legal configuration changes are covered too.

nodes.label: Draft/applied filter state pattern
nodes.rationale: Filters are kept in a `draft` state and only copied into the `filters` state when the 'Filtrar' button is pressed, so typing in the search box does not fire a request per keystroke; the effect depends on `filters`, not `draft`.

nodes.label: Endpoint instrumentation of ~45 mutating routes
nodes.rationale: Coverage is defined as 'every mutating endpoint', not a curated subset: the call is inserted just before the successful `return NextResponse.json(...)`, so the audit row is only written when the business mutation actually succeeded. The work is split into tasks by module so each group can be typechecked and committed on its own.

nodes.label: Best-effort audit logging (try/catch interno)
nodes.rationale: logActivity wraps the insert in its own try/catch with console.error and must never alter the flow or the response of the business mutation. Audit is secondary to the operation being audited: a missing/failing audit row is acceptable, a 500 caused by logging is not. There is an explicit test that logActivity does not throw when the table does not exist.

Accepted trade-off: `settings` is broader than ideal for legal data, but adding a `legal` key later is non-breaking, so the spec takes zero new permission plumbing now.

nodes.label: Fixed-PK Singleton Row Pattern (key='privacy_policy')
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.rationale: The user chose no public versioning and a single document, so legal identity data lives in one row with a fixed primary key. A fixed PK is simpler than a per-document table and deliberately mirrors the existing `brand_settings` key/value pattern in the schema; extra `key` values ('tos', 'cookies') can be added later without schema changes, keeping the multi-document legal hub a non-goal today but cheap to unlock.

nodes.label: Static Non-Editable Policy Body
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.rationale: Rich-text editing of the body is an explicit non-goal: the admin edits only the 8 variable fields while the legal text stays a React component that interpolates them, so compliance wording is reviewed in code. Trade-off accepted: fixing a bad OCR typo later requires a code change, mitigated by keeping the whole body in one file (`privacyPolicy.tsx`) for fast edits if Google still rejects the page.

nodes.label: actor_name Snapshot Column (nullable actor_id)
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.rationale: `actor_id` is nullable (null = anonymous public action, e.g. a booking from the wizard without a session) and `actor_name` is a denormalized snapshot so the log stays readable after the user is renamed or deleted. Denormalization over a join is a deliberate readability/durability trade-off for an audit table that is never rewritten.

nodes.label: Best-Effort Insert Policy (never break the mutation)
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.norm_label: best-effort insert policy (never break the mutation)
nodes.rationale: The audit insert is wrapped in try/catch with a silent console.error so a log failure never breaks an already-committed business mutation nor changes the client response. Audit observability is explicitly subordinated to data integrity: the log is best-effort, and `metadata` serialization failures degrade to null instead of throwing.

nodes.label: Forward-Only, Unlimited Retention Decision
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.rationale: Scope decision from brainstorming: no backfill of past actions and no retention limit (indefinite growth in `activity_logs`). Reads are also out of scope — only mutations are recorded, which keeps the write surface at the ~45 mutating endpoints and the log cheap to append to.

nodes.label: Pre-existing Partial Trails (cancelled_appointments, inventory_movements, created_by)
nodes.community_name: Módulo legal y política de privacidad
nodes.rationale: The module exists because the system had only scattered, module-local traces of who changed what (the `cancelled_appointments` archive, the `inventory_movements` kardex, dispersed `created_by` columns) and no persistent record of who made each change. The response is one generic table plus a manual `logActivity()` call per endpoint — chosen over a generic middleware/ORM-hook approach, trading explicitness per route for no runtime interception layer.

nodes.label: Graphify --code-Only Indexing (avoids API keys)
nodes.rationale: The project runs graphify with --code-only so no GEMINI_API_KEY is required for semantic extraction; the accepted trade-off is that .md documents are not indexed into the graph.

nodes.label: Windows Shell Command Rules
nodes.rationale: PowerShell 5.1 has no && operator, so commands chain with 'cmd1; if ($?) { cmd2 }'; paths with spaces need double quotes, binaries run via the call operator, and full cmdlets (Get-ChildItem, Remove-Item) are preferred over ls/rm aliases.

nodes.label: Privacy Policy Legal Module
nodes.rationale: Goal: ship a public, server-rendered /politicas page backed by a Drizzle singleton row, plus an admin CRUD module at /dashboard/legal to edit the variable fields of the policy. Architecture explicitly scopes out body editing, versioning and multi-document support: a static Spanish body component interpolates 9 stored values, the module can grow to more legal documents later but this plan ships a single document.

nodes.label: Value placeholder interpolation contract
nodes.rationale: The plan enumerates exactly where each stored value is substituted in the Spanish body (companyName in the definitions, 'Sitio web' and 'Contáctenos'; siteUrl in the website definition; country and governingLaw in 'Ley que Rige'; the three contact fields in 'Contáctenos'; effectiveDate in the 'Actualizado el' header and footer). Optional contactPhone/contactUrl render conditionally so a missing value never prints 'undefined'.

nodes.label: PrivacyPolicyValues as single source of truth
nodes.norm_label: privacypolicyvalues as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Self-review requirement 3: PrivacyPolicyValues is declared once and reused by the types file, the defaults, the body component, the public API response, the admin API validation, the public page and the admin form, so all layers agree on the same field names.

nodes.label: Manual + lint + tsc verification instead of an automated suite
nodes.norm_label: manual + lint + tsc verification instead of an automated suite
nodes.rationale: The project has no automated test suite at the time of the plan, so correctness is proven with npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint and a scripted manual smoke test in dev plus a production build, including a logged-out visit to /politicas to prove the public route stays unauthenticated.

nodes.label: legal_settings singleton-row storage pattern
nodes.rationale: The legal document is stored as a singleton row whose primary key is fixed to the literal 'privacy_policy'. The key column is the seam that lets the module grow to more legal documents later without a schema migration, while the current plan ships a single document.

nodes.label: Split public-read vs permission-gated admin-write API
nodes.norm_label: split public-read vs permission-gated admin-write api
nodes.rationale: Public routes must not require authentication while admin routes must, so the module is split into two endpoints over the same singleton row: GET /api/legal/privacy is intentionally unauthenticated, and GET/PUT /api/admin/legal/privacy is gated by hasPermission(session, 'settings').

nodes.label: Static body + interpolated values (no rich-text editing)
nodes.norm_label: static body + interpolated values (no rich-text editing)
nodes.rationale: The policy body is hard-coded Spanish JSX, faithful to the OCR'd source with 13 documented typo corrections, and only the variable values are admin-editable. Trade-off: the legal substance cannot be changed from the dashboard, but the body stays reviewable, typed and free of any HTML injection surface.

nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: bloqueo de edicion de una factura con pagos asociados
nodes.rationale: Si la factura tiene supplier_payments, PATCH rechaza cambiar type, currency, totalUsd o items (400) y solo deja editar proveedor, categoria, numero, fechas y notas; DELETE devuelve 400 pidiendo borrar antes los pagos. WHY: los pagos congelan el monto, y mutar el total dejaria pagos mayores que la factura con un estado 'paid' falso. BillFormDialog replica el bloqueo en la UI (banner ambar y botones de tipo/moneda deshabilitados).

nodes.label: Reglas de borrado referencial de compras e inventario
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: reglas de borrado referencial de compras e inventario
nodes.rationale: Ningun DELETE de proveedor, categoria, banco, factura o producto de inventario cuelga en cascada sobre datos historicos: cada uno cuenta las filas dependientes y devuelve 400 sugiriendo 'desactivalo en su lugar' (o 'elimina primero los pagos' en facturas). WHY: better-sqlite3 no tiene ON DELETE RESTRICT y un borrado libre romperia el P&L y el kardex. La unica cascada permitida es bill_items -> bills, porque las lineas no tienen existencia propia.

nodes.label: Uso de productos por servicio como dato informativo (estUsos)
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: uso de productos por servicio como dato informativo (estusos)
nodes.rationale: service_products NO descuenta stock automaticamente: solo alimenta estUsos = stock / suma de quantity_per_service como estimacion de cuantos servicios saldran del inventario actual. WHY: el consumo real de insumos varia por clienta y por diseno, asi que automatizarlo produciria stock negativo; es una ayuda a la compra, no una contabilidad de consumo. PUT /api/service-products borra y reinserta el mapeo completo del servicio para que la UI no tenga que hacer diffs.

nodes.label: Las facturas de inventario se registran siempre en USD
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: las facturas de inventario se registran siempre en usd
nodes.rationale: POST /api/bills devuelve 400 si type='inventory' y currency != 'USD'. WHY: los costos unitarios alimentan el promedio ponderado en USD, y aceptar Bs convertiria el costo con una tasa arbitraria y ensuciaria el valor del inventario. La excepcion son las facturas type='fixed' (alquiler, servicios basicos), que si admiten Bs con rate.

nodes.label: Patron de auth por endpoint (auth() + isAdmin -> 401)
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: patron de auth por endpoint (auth() + isadmin -> 401)
nodes.rationale: Todos los endpoints nuevos repiten 'const session = await auth(); if (!(await isAdmin(session))) return 401' y las paginas admin hacen redirect('/') en el server component. WHY: en esta fase solo existe el rol admin (los permisos granulares llegan despues) y la guarda va en el endpoint, no solo en la pagina, porque los datos de finanzas son los mas sensibles del sistema.

nodes.label: Kardex de inventario (bitacora de movimientos)
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.rationale: Toda mutacion de stock escribe una fila en inventory_movements con kind in|out|adjust, cantidad con signo, ref_type bill|manual y ref_id, para que el stock actual sea derivable de la bitacora. WHY: ref_type separa los movimientos automaticos de factura de los manuales, y la reversion de una factura NO borra el historial: inserta un 'out' negativo con nota 'Reversion de factura'.

nodes.label: P&L mensual base caja (servicios del mes vs gastos del mes)
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: p&l mensual base caja (servicios del mes vs gastos del mes)
nodes.rationale: Ingresos = suma de service_purchases.service_price de citas status='completed' cuyo start_time cae en el mes; gastos = suma de bills.total_usd por bill_date en el mes. WHY: se usa el snapshot de service_purchases (no el precio actual de services) para que el historico no cambie si el admin edita precios, y las citas completadas para contar solo lo realmente producido. monthRange se exporta desde financials.ts porque GET /api/bills?month= necesita el mismo rango, y todo se ancla con dateTimeToTs en America/Caracas.

nodes.label: Multi-moneda USD/VES con totalUsd = amountVes / rate
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.norm_label: multi-moneda usd/ves con totalusd = amountves / rate
nodes.rationale: Facturas de gasto fijo y pagos a proveedores se guardan en USD o Bs mas la tasa del dia, y totalUsd = round(amountVes / rate, 2) es la unica columna que consume el P&L. WHY: se guardan tambien amountVes y rate por fila para no perder el monto original ni congelar la conversion cuando la tasa cambie despues. recomputeBillStatus usa un margen de 0.004 para absorber el error de punto flotante de las sumas.

nodes.label: Costo promedio ponderado de inventario
nodes.community_name: API de compras, inventario y financieros
nodes.rationale: El avg_cost se recalcula en CADA entrada con (stock*avgCost + qty*unitCost)/newStock, redondeado a 4 decimales, y si el stock llega a 0 vuelve a ser el unitCost de la ultima entrada. WHY: los costos unitarios de los insumos alimentan el promedio ponderado en USD; un salon pequeno que no tiene Purchase Price Valuation por lotes (FIFO) necesita un costo de reposicion realista para calcular stockValue.

nodes.label: Rationale: auto-generated product code (PRD-<n>)
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.rationale: Requiring a valid product code blocked creating items from the bill/complete-appointment dialogs, so the code became optional and the server derives the next PRD-<n> by scanning existing ids; the UI placeholder changed to 'Código (opcional, se genera solo)' and the button is now gated only on the name.

nodes.label: Rationale: category/subcategory nail-polish taxonomy
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.rationale: Nail polish does not consume stock linearly, so a two-level taxonomy (category e.g. 'Esmalte', subcategory e.g. 'Max Glow') is what makes the 'which polishes did we use in this appointment' picker usable; items without a category are deliberately filtered out of that picker.

nodes.label: Rationale: exhausted flag + max uses auto-decrement
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.norm_label: rationale: exhausted flag + max uses auto-decrement
nodes.rationale: A polish bottle dies after N appointments, not when a computed quantity hits zero, so uses_consumed is incremented per recorded usage and is_exhausted flips automatically once uses_consumed >= max_uses; manual setExhausted/reopen exists because the count is often wrong in practice, and marking exhausted forces stock to 0 with an adjust movement so the kardex stays truthful.

nodes.label: Rationale: unique (appointment_id, inventory_item_id) upsert
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.rationale: The unique index plus onConflictDoUpdate makes usage entry idempotent: re-submitting the completion PATCH updates the quantity instead of double-decrementing stock, while each recorded use still produces exactly one 'out' movement with ref_type='usage'.

nodes.label: Rationale: avg_cost corrections audited in the kardex
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.norm_label: rationale: avg_cost corrections audited in the kardex
nodes.rationale: Weighted average cost can be wrong when a purchase is forgotten, and silently editing avg_cost destroys the audit trail. The correction writes a quantity=0 'cost_adjust' row carrying the new unitCostUsd plus a mandatory reason, so who changed the cost and why is visible in the kardex; it is gated behind the adjustInventory permission (canAdjustInventory) separately from the inventory permission.

nodes.label: Rationale: optional payment/supplier-payment reference
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.rationale: Cash and card payments have no bank transfer reference, so the NOT NULL column and the 400 guards were removed (reference is normalized to null) and the mandatory asterisk was dropped from the payment dialogs. The photoUrl guard on supplier payments is deliberately kept because the capture is the only proof of the transfer.

nodes.label: Rationale: photoUrl capture stays mandatory for supplier payments
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.norm_label: rationale: photourl capture stays mandatory for supplier payments
nodes.rationale: Feature 1 only relaxes the reference; the photoUrl validation in the API and in SupplierPaymentDialog must stay intact, so the plan re-verifies it as an explicit non-regression check.

nodes.label: Rationale: service already performed, with no appointment
nodes.community_name: Uso de inventario por cita y agotado
nodes.norm_label: rationale: service already performed, with no appointment
nodes.rationale: Walk-ins and retrospective corrections had no way to enter accounts receivable because service_purchases required an appointment row. appointment_id becomes nullable, the row is an immutable snapshot (serviceName/Price/DurationMins copied) created as financialStatus 'pending', and price overrides are capped at 150% of list price; the insert immediately re-runs recomputeFinancialStatus + applyPaidToClient and bumps totalVisits so balances stay consistent.

nodes.label: CRM de clientes (users con role='client')
nodes.community_name: Fotos de citas, galería y servicios
nodes.rationale: No hay tabla `clients`: los clientes son filas de `users` con `role='client'`, de modo que el alta manual reutiliza la autenticación existente. El alta genera un email placeholder `<uuid>@local` y un `bcrypt.hash(crypto.randomUUID(), 10)` porque un walk-in no tiene email ni contraseña real; se devuelve 409 si el email ya existe. La búsqueda es server-side por `LIKE` sobre nombre/email/teléfono y el panel edita contacto y notas técnicas (techNotes).

nodes.rationale: El teléfono es obligatorio para el contacto por WhatsApp pero Google OAuth no lo provee, así que se inyecta `phone` en el JWT y en la sesión y se fuerza el paso con guardas de redirect en `/profile` y `/book` (si no hay teléfono → `/complete-registration`), en vez de confiar en que el usuario lo escriba. La página redirige a `/profile` si ya tiene teléfono, y `/profile` se reserva para usuarios ya contactables.

nodes.label: Muro de inspiración (gallery alimentado por fotos finales)
nodes.community_name: Fotos de citas, galería y servicios
nodes.norm_label: muro de inspiracion (gallery alimentado por fotos finales)
nodes.rationale: El muro se alimenta de las fotos `kind='final'` de citas con `sharedToGallery=1`, no de una tabla de galería propia: así una foto publicada es exactamente la foto que la manicurista subió al completar la cita. La respuesta de `GET /api/gallery` es a nivel de foto (`item.id` = id de la foto, no de la cita) y pagina por cursor `createdAt`, que es lo que permite que `GalleryGrid` abra una foto concreta y CTA 'agendar similar'.

nodes.community_name: Fotos de citas, galería y servicios
nodes.norm_label: seleccion de modelos de inspiracion al confirmar la reserva
nodes.rationale: El paso 3 del wizard embebe una mini-galería (`GET /api/gallery?limit=50`) y acumula `selectedModels` (URLs). Las URLs del muro y las subidas por la clienta se combinan en una sola lista `urlsToSend = [...referencePhotoUrls, ...selectedModels]`, de la que además sale `referencePhotoUrl: urlsToSend[0]` para la columna legacy: una sola lista evita dos campos que puedan divergir.

El home hace el mismo agrupado en su Server Component; `ServiceCard` cae a un placeholder cuando el servicio no tiene fotos.

nodes.label: Tabla service_photos (fotos de catálogo)
nodes.community_name: Fotos de citas, galería y servicios
nodes.rationale: Las fotos de catálogo no pertenecen a ninguna cita, así que no pueden vivir en `appointment_photos`: necesitan su propia tabla con FK a `services` y `onDelete: 'cascade'`. `position` conserva el orden del carrusel; la asignación de posiciones en el POST continúa desde `max(position)+1` en vez de renumerar, por lo que las fotos ya numeradas no se desplazan al añadir.

nodes.label: Soft Delete (status='cancelled') Removal
nodes.rationale: Soft delete left two sources of truth (a 'cancelled' row plus the archive). It is removed entirely: PATCH returns 400 telling callers to use DELETE, the now-dead cancellation block is deleted and the POST /cancel route is removed, making DELETE the single cancellation path.

nodes.label: slots.ts Pure Availability Function
nodes.rationale: Availability is a pure function of (date, duration, existing appointments, blockouts) returning 9am-6pm slots, so it can be shared by the booking wizard and the server without a DB round trip inside the function.

nodes.label: /api/blockouts CRUD (No Available Time Blocks)
nodes.rationale: Blockouts are managed from the agenda (grey block with a reason and an 'x' to delete in day view, marked as unavailable in week view). Accepted edge case: blocks are not validated against each other, only appointment creation validates against them.

nodes.label: slots.ts generateSlots + getWorkingHoursForDate
nodes.rationale: The OPEN/CLOSE constants are replaced by openTime/closeTime parameters and getWorkingHoursForDate reads the weekday row; hour-aligned slots and duration-based closing are preserved. A closed day returns slots: [] and the UI shows 'Cerrado'.

nodes.label: Admin-Created Appointments for Walk-ins (clientId field)
nodes.rationale: POST /api/appointments used to force clientId = session.user.id, so the salon could never book a client without an account. An optional clientId now requires isAdmin; without it the public flow is unchanged, and admin-created appointments start with status 'pending'.

nodes.label: working_hours Table (Per Weekday Open/Close)
nodes.rationale: The 09:00-18:00 window was hardcoded in src/lib/slots.ts; moving it to day_of_week rows lets the admin edit the schedule. A missing row falls back to the default (Mon-Sat open, Sunday closed) so availability is not broken before the seed runs.

nodes.label: availability.ts isSlotAvailable (Single Source of Truth)
nodes.rationale: Before this, the client-side slot list was the only availability check, so double bookings were possible. The rule (no overlap with pending/confirmed appointments or blockouts, inside working hours, not in the past) is extracted into availability.ts and used by both POST /api/appointments and /api/slots.

nodes.label: GET /api/balances (Clients with balanceUsd > 0)
nodes.rationale: Only role='client' users with a positive rounded balance are listed, ordered by debt descending, with totalUsd as the sum of all debts. A negative balance never happens: overpayment is not shown as negative debt, only the CRM balance can read 0.

nodes.label: payments Table (Accounts Receivable Payments)
nodes.rationale: appointments.appointment_id is nullable ON DELETE SET NULL on purpose: if a cancelled appointment is deleted the payment survives, unlinked. Dual currency is stored as amount_usd plus optional amount_ves/rate, with amountUsd = round(amountVes / rate, 2), keeping the Bs amount and rate for audit. reference is mandatory.

nodes.label: /api/payments CRUD (Admin)
nodes.rationale: Partial payments (abonos) are allowed and payments without an appointment are allowed as a general credit; deleting a wrong payment changes nothing but the balance, which is recomputed.

nodes.label: Payment Section inside CompleteAppointmentDialog
nodes.rationale: Agreed decision 3: debt is born when the appointment is completed — if the admin does not mark it as paid, the receivable appears automatically; if paid, the dialog posts the payment inline (amount defaults to the service price, currency $ or Bs, rate auto/editable, mandatory reference).

nodes.label: Live Balance Rule (no separate accounting ledger)
nodes.norm_label: live balance rule (no separate accounting ledger)
nodes.rationale: Agreed decision 4: saldo = sum(completed appointment snapshot prices) - sum(payments), computed live; a receivable is not a row, and no separate accounting ledger is introduced. The amount owed per appointment comes from service_purchases.service_price (the snapshot the admin can edit in the CRM), never from services.price.

nodes.label: service_purchases.service_price as Balance Basis
nodes.rationale: The debt must reflect the price the client actually agreed to (the immutable snapshot taken at purchase), so services.price is deliberately not used for balances.

nodes.label: Orphan Payments Allowed (appointment_id -> NULL)
nodes.rationale: A cancelled appointment with payments is still deletable: payments.appointment_id becomes NULL thanks to ON DELETE SET NULL and the balance is unaffected, because only completed appointments count toward the debt.
